headline: Eighty-One Plays, One Hundred Eighty-Three Dollars, Zero Excuses
paragraphs: Week 4 got graded in real time, no box scores peeking over the model's shoulder, and the result was a bloodbath. It looked at 71 games, found something it liked in 46 of them, passed on 25, and fired off 81 plays at $10 each. Final tally: 31-48-2 for a loss of $183.21, an ROI of minus 22.6 percent. The model expected to win 59.5 percent of these. It won 39.2 percent.

The moneyline is where the wheels detached and rolled into a ditch. Twenty plays, 5-15, minus $89.55, an ROI of minus 44.8 percent, and the model walked in expecting 51 percent. Spreads went 18-21-1 for minus $46.38 and totals went 8-12-1 for minus $47.28, so nothing was healthy, but the moneylines were the ones actively setting money on fire. Texas A&M at +290 was the loudest, 15.2 points of claimed edge, final score LSU 35, Texas A&M 6.

There were two nights of genuine brilliance in there. Iowa 20, Michigan 19 paid off three ways, including Over 38.5 at a 7.6 point edge and Iowa moneyline at +180 for a tidy $18. Cincinnati moneyline at +200 returned $20 out of a 31-26 win. The published top five, the plays actually put in front of readers, went 1-4 for minus $30.91 and an ROI of minus 61.8 percent. That one stings differently.

For context on how little the market agreed: 51 plays saw their line move, and only 20 of them, 39.2 percent, moved toward the model. One week graded for real, one season record of 31-48-2, minus $183.21 on $810 staked. The hindsight week sitting in the archive at 40-25-1 and plus $110.47 can stay there looking pretty. It never had to guess.
